claims.text: Introducing Mn or Fe into a ceria–zirconia support creates an abundance of oxygen vacancies.
Dopant-induced oxygen vacancies anchor Pt nanoparticles more effectively than an undoped ceria–zirconia support.
Optimized Mn or Fe doping enhances catalytic activity under automotive exhaust conditions.
Optimized Mn or Fe doping enhances catalyst durability under automotive exhaust conditions.
The doped support can permit a significant reduction in platinum-group-metal loading.
A targeted dopant concentration of 5–10 mol% followed by calcination promotes oxygen-vacancy formation.
The proposed doped ceria–zirconia phase is enriched in oxygen vacancies.
Oxygen vacancies in the doped support act as strong anchoring sites for Pt nanoparticles.
Heteroatom doping increases the oxygen-storage capacity of ceria–zirconia.
Heteroatom doping stabilizes the dispersion of Pt nanoparticles.
Stabilized Pt dispersion reduces nanoparticle sintering during thermal cycling.
Reduced Pt sintering maintains catalytic activity and durability while enabling lower Pt content.
The doped catalyst will produce around a 30% improvement in CO conversion relative to the undoped catalyst.
The doped catalyst will produce around a 30% improvement in hydrocarbon conversion relative to the undoped catalyst.
The doped catalyst will produce around a 30% improvement in NOx conversion relative to the undoped catalyst.
The doped catalyst will exhibit enhanced durability over extended thermal cycling relative to the undoped catalyst.
The anticipated benefits apply during rapid thermal cycling between 200°C and 800°C under alternating lean and rich operation.
Excessive dopant concentration could disrupt the intrinsic redox properties of the ceria–zirconia support.
The optimal dopant identity and concentration remain undetermined.
Failure of an optimally doped catalyst to achieve at least 30% greater conversion while maintaining superior Pt dispersion and durability relative to the undoped control would falsify the hypothesis.
